History of Present Illness:
___ year old female with h/o HTN, fibromyalgia, seizure disorder, 
presents with chief complaint of n/v for 6 days. Emesis is 
non-bloody, no coffee grounds, looks like food she has eaten or 
bilious. +Fever/chills-- highest temp at home was 100.8 2 days 
prior to admission. She has tried bowel rest and PO zofran 
without relief. She has had minimal to no PO intake for the past 
few days as she would vomit up anything that she tried to eat. 
Last ate small amount of soup the day prior to admission. Has 
not been able to take her meds for the past 3 days. Pt also 
reports urinary frequency and urgency x 5 days but no dysuria. 
Additionally, she complains of generalized increase in pain all 
over her body, consistent with her usual fibromyalgia pain. 
Denies diarrhea. Denies hematemesis or melena. Her brother has 
had a sore throat recently, no other sick contacts. Had one 
episode like this last year for which she reports no etiology 
was found and she improved on IVF.  
.  
In the ED, initial vs were: T 98.0, P 87, BP 156/87, R 16, O2 
sat 99% RA. She appeared dry on exam and had mild suprapubic 
tenderness. IV team was unable to get access (she is known to 
have difficult access) and so IJ was placed. Got 1L NS, IV 
zofran, IV morphine 2mg x ___ x 3 for pain. Also nicotine 
patch. No vomiting in the ED. Admitted to medicine for IV fluids 
and pain control.  
.  
On the floor, she complains of nausea and ___ pain in the 
joints in her hips, legs, and back.  
.

___: Abdominal X-ray
Three supine views of the abdomen were reviewed. There is no 
evidence of 
bowel obstruction. There is no air-fluid level. There is no free 
air below 
the diaphragm. Degenerative changes of the spine and the 
sacroiliac joints 
are demonstrated. 
IMPRESSION: No evidence of small-bowel obstruction. 
.
___: Abdominal X-ray
SUPINE ABDOMEN: There is a relative paucity of bowel gas 
centrally, without definite evidence of obstruction or ileus, as 
air and stool is seen throughout the colon. There is no supine 
evidence of free intraperitoneal air. There is no pneumatosis. 
Linear foci of calcifications are seen along the soft tissues of 
the lateral abdominal wall on the right, and may reflect either 
soft tissue calcifications, or may be external to the patient.  
IMPRESSION: No evidence of obstruction. 
 
Brief Hospital Course:
1. NAUSEA/VOMITING:
The concern initially was for a small bowel obstruction or ileus 
with this patient's narcotic use.  A negative KUB made this less 
likely.  Most likely etiology was a viral gastroenteritis or 
gastroparesis.  The patient was treated with IV Zofran, Reglan, 
Protonix and bowel rest.  Symptoms improved and over several 
days she was able to tolerate food and fluids.  She had minimal 
symptoms of nausea and vomiting on discharge.  She continued to 
have bowel movements throughout admission.
.
2. LEFT QUADRANT PAIN
On the day after admission, the patient developed a left lower 
quadrant pain which did not radiate.  She remained 
hemodynamically stable and afebrile.  It was recommended that 
she undergo a CT scan of the abdomen with IV and PO contrast, 
however due to lack of IV access she was unable to have IV 
contrast.  The patient had a central line placed in the internal 
jugular in the ED but this was not able to be used for her CT 
scan.  She would not attempt PO contrast due to fear of becoming 
more nauseous and vomiting.  Her left lower quadrant pain 
resolved over several days.  This may have been related to her 
fibromyalgia or musculoskeletal pain.
.
3. FIBROMYALGIA
The patient was initially put on IV pain medications due to her 
nausea and vomiting.  She was tried on IV Dilaudid which made 
her nausea worse so she was put on IV Morphine.  She was 
transitioned to PO Oxycodone and Morphine on the day after 
admission and fibromyalgia pain was controlled.  Narcotic pain 
medications were confirmed with her PCP who suggested that no 
changes be made to her pain regimen.  She was on Oxycodone 45mg 
PO q6hours and Morphine ___ 45mg PO q6hours PRN.  She was 
discharged with this regimen and no changes or escalation of 
pain medications were made.
.
HYPERTENSION
The patient was continued on her Nifedipine XL 60mg PO qday for 
her hypertension and blood pressure was controlled during this 
admission.
.
SEIZURE DISORDER
The patient was initially subtherapeutic on her phenytoin, 
___ from vomiting prior to admission.  She was initially put 
on IV Phenytoin 200mg, 200mg, 300mg q8 hours for total daily 
dose of 1000mg.  She was rechecked and levels were low so she 
was bolused 1000mg IV phenytoin.  Levels the following morning 
were therapeutic.  She was changed to her home dose of Phenytoin 
and will have her Phenytoin levels checked in 1 week.  She had 
no seizures while hospitalized.
.
HX OF DVT/PE
Ms. ___ was sub-therapeutic on her Coumadin on admission 
with an INR of 1.2.  She was restarted on her home dose of 
Coumadin 7.5mg and was discharged on this dose with instructions 
to have her labs rechecked in 1 week.  
.  
HYPOTHYROIDISM 
Patient was put initially on IV Levothyroxine 25mcg qday and 
then was transitioned to PO Levothyroxine 25mcg PO daily.  This 
was continued on discharge.
.  
TOBACCO ABUSE
The patient was put on a Nicotine patch for smoking cessation.  
At times she requested to leave the floor to smoke but was able 
to tolerate cravings with gum and did not leave the floor.
.
PROPHYLAXIS
She was given SC Heparin for DVT prophylaxis while 
sub-therapeutic on Coumadin.  She was put on her home dose of 
Omeprazole and a bowel regimen.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital with nausea and vomiting.  An 
abdominal x-ray did not show any obstruction.  You improved and 
were able to eat and drink on discharge.

You were started on Ciprofloxacin to take for a Urinary tract 
infection.  You should take this for 7 days.  You were started 
on Reglan 10mg three times a day.  You should take this 30 
minutes prior to meals to help with motility of the stomach.

You should call your doctor or come to the emergency room with 
any fevers > 101 degrees, chills, night sweats, intractable 
vomiting, worsening abdominal pain or bloating, blood in your 
bowel movements, diarrhea, leg swelling or any skin rashes.

Findings:

There is a left-sided internal jugular line seen in situ with the tip
approximately at the cavoatrial junction.  There is no pneumothorax.  The
cardiomediastinal silhouette is unremarkable.  The lungs are clear.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Nausea and vomiting, suspected small-bowel
obstruction.

Three supine views of the abdomen were reviewed.  There is no evidence of
bowel obstruction.  There is no air-fluid level.  There is no free air below
the diaphragm.  Degenerative changes of the spine and the sacroiliac joints
are demonstrated.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of small-bowel obstruction.
